results.title: Nebius to Increase GPU Rental Prices by 17-21% Starting October 1 | KuCoin
highlights:
# Nebius to Increase GPU Rental Prices by 17-21% Starting October 1

 MarsBit

Release Time: 2026/09/29 02:55:25

Nebius will increase on-demand GPU rental prices by 17–21% effective October 1, impacting models such as the H100, H200, B200, and B300. On-chain data indicates renewed interest in computing power leasing, with Maixinlin up over 18%. Traders are advised to monitor altcoins as the market responds to the price adjustment.

Huoxing Finance reports that the AI computing power leasing sector experienced intraday volatility and a rebound, with Maxinlin rising 20% to its daily limit. Previously, Nanwei Software achieved four gains in six trading days, while Chuangye Heima, Jiawang Technology, Hubei Radio and TV, Yingfeng Environment, and Dongfang Materials also rose. On the news front, computing power lessor Nebius plans to increase on-demand rental rates for key NVIDIA GPUs effective October 1: H100 will rise from $3.85 to $4.50 per hour, H200 from $4.50 to $5.40, B200 from $7.15 to $8.50, and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50—an overall increase of approximately 17% to 21%. (Caixin Global)

results.title: Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1. | Bobby Clay
highlights:
# Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1. | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-09-29T00:00:00+00:00

...

Nebius sets the cheapest published H100 across the nine providers we track at $3.85 per GPU-hour. It has posted an increase to $4.50 for October 1.

Nebius is adding 65 cents to its own rate. The cheapest published H100 across those nine goes up five cents, from $3.85 to $3.90, because Crusoe is next at $3.90 in US East (New York), then Lambda $3.99 in the same September 27 catalog.

Sixty-five cents at one provider, five cents on the board, and Nebius drops from first to third. Nothing else on the published side moved. Not one rate we compared changed more than 1%, and the four floors on our board have not moved since August 24.

The traded market did move. The Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index built from actual transactions, settled A100 SXM4 at $0.91 on September 28, the lowest weekly reading we have recorded since May 18. B200 settled at $8.11, the highest.

If you are renewing H100 or A100, that index is your lever. The traded price is now below every rate published across those nine. On H100 it settled at $2.56 against the cheapest rate published across those nine at $3.85, a gap of $1.29 that was $1.06 a week earlier. The list price is not your anchor.

One limit worth stating. A published rate is an asking price and a posted rate is an intention. Our September 27 capture of the Nebius catalog was identical to September 21, so the October 1 rates are published and not yet observed. And the $6.69 B200 listing that sets the floor across those nine is Lambda's, which names no region this week.

results.title: GPU rental prices are going up, not down. | Peter Lee
highlights:
GPU rental prices are going up, not down.

Nebius raises rates October 1 — its second hike in three months:
• H100: +17%
• H200: +20%
• B200: +19%
• B300: +21%

Wall Street just split wide open on what it means. JPMorgan upgraded CoreWeave to Overweight ($125 target): pricing power, not debt, is the story — short-term compute now sells at a steep premium, some rivals at ~3x long-term rates.

Days earlier, Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated both CoreWeave and Nebius at Sell, calling neocloud earnings "cyclically inflated."
Both can't be right about durability. But both agree on the present: compute is a seller's market.

results.title: Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) Hikes AI Compute Prices By Up To 21%, Signaling Deepening GPU Supply Crunch
highlights:
Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) is raising on-demand hourly rates for four Nvidia GPU models by between 17% and 21%, effective October 1, 2026.

The price increases cover four of Nvidia’s most sought-after chips: the H100, H200, B200, and B300, along with Nebius’ CPU-only server offerings.

The October 1 round is not the first increase this year, with Nebius having already raised rates substantially since early May.

In May, the older H100 chip was priced at $2.95 per hour and the B300 at $6.10, but after this latest round those same chips will cost $4.50 and $9.50 respectively.

That represents cumulative increases of roughly 53% and 56% on those two chips alone over a span of just five months.

Notably, rising prices for the H100, a chip that predates Nvidia’s current Blackwell generation, may say more about the depth of the supply shortage than any premium on the newest hardware.

When a company is expanding capacity at speed, conventional logic suggests it should be working to fill that capacity, not charging customers more for it.

Management has indicated it could sell all of its 2027 capacity today on the terms of its most recent contracts, underscoring just how acute demand for AI compute has become.

The aggressive build-out has required substantial financing, including $5.75 billion in convertible notes sold in August and approximately $2.8 billion in new shares sold through June.

Shortage pricing can reverse quickly if supply catches up with demand, and Nebius and its rivals continue to add capacity at a rapid pace, which could put downward pressure on hourly rates.

The October 1 price hike is described as a strong signal of market tightness rather than a primary revenue driver, given that new rates apply to a smaller share of Nebius’ overall business than the headline numbers suggest.

results.title: Nvidia B200 Price Hits $8.01/Hr as GPU Costs Diverge
highlights:
Renting a Nvidia B200 by the hour has no single market price, because Nvidia does not sell it by the GPU-hour and each cloud sets its own rate. Listings in November 2026 reportedly run from $4.11 per GPU-hour, the lowest listed on-demand rate, at Beam Cloud to $16.11 per GPU-hour. Google Cloud listed $16.11 on demand in us-west1 on November 6. Treat any single average, including one quoted from the SemiAnalysis GPU pricing index, as a snapshot to check against provider pages. The B200 is listed as available for rental across multiple cloud providers as of November 6, 2026, and its status is active. It is no longer the only Blackwell option: HGX B300 systems based on Blackwell Ultra became generally available on Google Distributed Cloud air-gapped deployments on October 20, 2026, and Vera Rubin NVL72 is marked early access. Older B200 snapshots, H100 and H200 prices, and any one provider’s rate should not be read as the current market-wide B200 price. Check each provider’s current terms before you commit.

...

The core data point comes from the SemiAnalysis GPU pricing index, which tracks day-to-day cloud rental rates across a basket of providers. In late September 2026, that index put B200 rental pricing at $8.01 per GPU-hour, a 79% climb from where it sat three months earlier. That figure is a market average rather than a price Nvidia publishes or any single provider charges, and a separate October 2026 report from Uvik put B200 median rental pricing at $8.19/GPU-hour across 9 providers, a similar level measured a different way. The same analysis calculated that a B200 now costs 21% more per unit of compute than an H100, a full reversal from June 2026, when a B200 was actually 18% cheaper than an H100 on the same compute-adjusted basis.

...

That detail is the thread running through this entire pricing episode.

...

| GPU | Generation | HBM Memory | Cloud Rental (per GPU-hour) | Indicative Hardware Price | Approx. Cost per GB |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 | Hopper | 80 GB HBM3 | Baseline (index reference) | ~$31,000 | ~$387.50/GB |
| H200 | Hopper | 141 GB HBM3e | ~1.76x H100 rate | ~$39,999 | ~$283.68/GB |
| B200 | Blackwell | 180 GB HBM3e | $8.01/hr (+21% vs H100 compute-adjusted) | ~$50,000–$70,000 | Not listed |

...

In February 2025, GPUTracker listed B200 spot pricing at $1.67/hour from Verda. In February 2025, GPUTracker listed B200 on-demand pricing at $3.40/hour from Vast.ai, and it listed Lambda’s B200 on-demand price at $3.99/hour. It also listed GB200 on-demand pricing at $6.50/hour from CoreWeave in February 2025.

...

Cloud providers themselves are caught in the middle. Neoclouds like CoreWeave, which made HGX B200 instances generally available in May 2025, and Lambda Labs, which built businesses around reselling Nvidia capacity, have to pass through higher acquisition costs or eat margin. Some have already chosen the former: Nebius, one of the higher-profile AI-cloud operators, raised its own pricing in 2026 citing rising memory costs, and it reportedly lifted its B200 on-demand rate from $7.15 to $8.50 per GPU-hour on October 1, 2026, a move and a price level that line up directly with the HBM scarcity driving the B200 and H200 numbers here.

results.title:
Dutch IT Channel
							-
				Nebius stelt prijzen voor Nvidia-chips H100 en B300 opwaarts bij
highlights:
Het verhuren van AI-rekenkracht in Europa wordt duurder. De in Nederland gevestigde AI-infrastructuuraanbieder Nebius verhoogt per 1 oktober 2026 de uurprijzen voor het huren van GPU's met 17 tot 21 procent. Dit blijkt uit de nieuwste Europese GPU-prijsindex van het onafhankelijke AI-onderzoeksbureau Lindstead. 

 

Door de prijsherziening stijgt het tarief voor een Nvidia H100 bij Nebius van circa 3,38 euro naar 3,95 euro per uur. De nieuwste generatie chips, de B300, gaat in prijs omhoog van ongeveer 6,88 euro naar 8,33 euro per uur. De prijsstijging past binnen een bredere ontwikkeling in de markt: de mediane huurprijs van een H200-GPU steeg in een jaar tijd met ongeveer 25 procent, waarbij elke nieuwe chipgeneratie duurder is per uur dan de voorgaande.
